C-46, ss. 462.31 and 83.02-83.3; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of origin (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations, Companies House, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's state of origin, or Canadian consular legalization where the state is not an Apostille Convention party; accompanied by a certified French translation by an OCCQ-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the general partner's constitutive documents (certificate of incorporation or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or statutory declaration of authenticity before a notary, followed by consular legalization if required; certified French translation mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport or national identity document for each natural-person UBO and the general partner's authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the document's country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-Canadian originals (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State apostille); certified French translation of any non-French text

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Power of Attorney (procuration) appointing the designated attorney for service in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the partner's jurisdiction, or the general partner's board resolution notarized in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the state of origin (if foreign) and mandatory certified French translation by an OCCQ-certified translator; notarization before a Quebec notary for the signature if executed in Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-owner declaration schedule (Déclaration de renseignements sur les bénéficiaires ultimes) for filing with the Registraire des entreprises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner of the limited partnership, with individual UBO attestations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the general partner or its authorized attorney; no apostille required for domestic filing, but foreign UBO identification documents require apostille and certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening aligned with FINTRAC guidance under the PCMLTFA: all natural-person general partners, every beneficial owner holding 25% or more, and each designated banking signatory must be screened at formation and on a continuous risk-based cycle against the Canadian Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada, the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) regulations, the United Nations Act consolidated sanctions, the OFSI list and provincial securities watchlists, with supplemental cross-reference to the U.S. OFAC SDN List and UK HM Treasury consolidated list where any counterparty has a U.S. or U.K. nexus. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of state, senior politicians, judges, military officers and their family members and close associates, must be identified under the FINTRAC regulatory glossary, flagged, and subject to enhanced due diligence. Notwithstanding the banking_aml_risk_tier of Low_Risk_Standard for the EdTech subscription model, no simplified exemption applies; baseline CDD, adverse-media review, and corroboration of the source of funds for the initial capital contribution remain mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Office of the Enterprise Registrar) - secure electronic portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French-language primacy is statutory under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business. The legal name of the limited partnership must be rendered in French; a non-French commercial designation may be used only in association with a French version and can never override the French legal name. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into Roman characters and phonetically adapted into French. All registration declarations and appended documents must be in French, and any foreign-language document must be accompanied by a certified translation delivered by a member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OCCQ).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Trust, Fiducie, Prêt, Loan - reserved for institutions authorized by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
Assurance, Insurance, Assurance-vie - requires prior authorization of the AMF
Université, University, Collège, École, Académie, Institut - requires authorization of the Ministère de l'Éducation when implying a recognized educational establishment
Royal, Royale, Gouvernement, Government, Municipal, Commission, Bureau officiel - implies affiliation with the Crown or a public authority and is generally refused
Coopérative, Coop - reserved for entities validly constituted as cooperatives under Quebec law
Any token creating confusion with an existing name in the Registraire database, prohibited under art. 15.2 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
Misleading tokens that falsely suggest the entity's form (e.g., 'Société par actions', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'SA') or that inaccurately describe the business purpose
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal from the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may, within 30 days of receipt, file a request for reconsideration, addressing the grounds enumerated in art. 15.2 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (confusion, prohibited matter, false or misleading indication). Reconsideration is decided in writing without additional cost. Should the refusal be maintained, the applicant may either (i) apply for a discretionary authorization demonstrating distinctive prior use or a registered trademark under the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, or (ii) institute judicial review before the Court of Québec (administrative division) within 30 days of the final written decision. Alternatively, the applicant may refile the reservation immediately with a modified name that preserves the distinctive element, thereby restarting the 90-day reservation window without the need for an appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or post-office box alone is not acceptable for the statutory registered office. Quebec law requires a fixed, physical civic address designated as the establishment (établissement) within Quebec, at which document service may lawfully be effected. An administrative-only physical suite operated by a law firm or licensed registered-agent service is permissible provided it is a real, verifiable street-level location and a natural person is designated as attorney for service. The remote-first EdTech subscription model does not derogate from this requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Probability_Compliance_Monitoring_Risk: estimated 5-10% likelihood of a physical presence verification by the Registraire des entreprises or an unannounced onsite 'audit sur place' by Revenu Québec within the first three years of operation for a low-risk EdTech subscription business. Probability increases if GST/QST registration anomalies, cross-border intercompany payments, or UBO declaration discrepancies trigger automated red-flag scoring in Revenu Québec's risk engine.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2273 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 6, 20-39 and applicable regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Business Registrar), Direction de la publicité légale des entreprises, Registre des entreprises du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed through the Registraire's online electronic service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and no escrow account requirement exists under the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF COMPASS EDWORKS LIMITED PARTNERSHIP. WHEREAS the undersigned general partner filed the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; RESOLVED: FIRST, the Partnership Agreement tabled before this meeting is adopted and ratified in full. SECOND, the registered office is established at 250, rue Saint-Antoine Ouest, Suite 300, Montréal, Québec H2Y 0A3, and the Registrar is instructed to record that address. THIRD, the general partner's representative is appointed Chief Operating Officer with authority to execute banking, subscription, regulatory filing, and payment-rail documents. FOURTH, all formation filings are confirmed, and the general partner is authorized to operate an interactive language-education software business in Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name search and reservation service at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name search in the REQ index to ensure the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing legal person or partnership name. If desired, file an online name reservation request. The name must comply with the Charter of the French Language and be distinctive; include a French generic term such as 'langues' or 'formation'. After approval, retain the reservation receipt, valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Requested corporate name in French and English
Identification of the general partner and each limited partner or their representatives
Description of principal activities (interactive language-learning software)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name request within 15 days; remedy deficiencies by adding a distinguishing element or adjusting the French-language designation, then re-file the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private deed executed before two witnesses or notarial act; no government approval required for the contractual formation stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in accordance with Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236-2273, naming the entity as 'société en commandite'; identify the general partner (which may be a single-member Canadian corporation) and limited partners; specify contributions, profit-sharing, management authority, dissolution events, and transfer restrictions. Execute the deed before a notary for additional evidentiary certainty or privately before two witnesses and record the act date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate status of the general partner, if corporate, issued by the incorporating authority
Identification and provincial or territorial corporate documents of each partner
List of capital contributions and valuation basis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the partnership agreement by supplementary deed; if registration has already been completed, file an amended declaration (déclaration modificative) with the Registraire to reflect the change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online electronic module 'Déclaration d'immatriculation (société en commandite)'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the Registraire's secure portal and complete the declaration screens: enter the partnership's name, registered office address in Québec, the general partner's name and registration number, limited partners' names and domiciles if declared, and a statement that the partnership is a limited partnership governed by the Civil Code of Québec. Attest accuracy, pay the registration fee by credit card, and digitally submit. The effective registration date is the submission date.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address (lease, authorization letter from owner, or utility bill)
Name reservation receipt (if obtained)
Registration number or identifier of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire queries the dossier, correct and resubmit the declaration through the same portal; if a material deficiency exists, file a supplementary declaration (déclaration modificative) and, where necessary, apply for discretionary relief under s. 42 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec - Mon dossier entreprise (online business account) and Registraire des entreprises du Québec for the NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued upon registration, create a Revenu Québec business account and enrol for GST/HST and QST accounts; obtain the tax account numbers. Register for payroll deductions if the partnership will hire employees. Confirm the date of commencement of activities and provide the partnership's mailing address and banking coordinates. Enrol for partnership informational returns for the first fiscal year and establish the quarterly or annual filing calendar.
required_dossiers: NEQ and Declaration of Registration number
General partner's name and residential or corporate address
Date of commencement of commercial activities
Bank account details
Description of subscription-based EdTech services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If enrolment is rejected, verify the legal name and address recorded at the Registraire, correct discrepancies, and resubmit; request a waiver of late-registration penalties under Revenu Québec's administrative remission policy where failure was due to clerical error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Registered Office Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Schedule I bank (BMO, RBC, Scotiabank, TD, CIBC, or National Bank) commercial banking desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the Declaration of Registration issued by the Registraire, the partnership agreement, the general partner's resolution, and identification of all signing officers; complete Know-Your-Client and beneficial ownership forms under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Open operating and settlement accounts to receive Apple IAP and Google Play Billing remittances in USD or CAD, and confirm the registered office address for receipt of legal correspondence.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Declaration of Registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
Original or notarial copy of the partnership agreement
General partner's authorization resolution
Corporate registry extract of the general partner, if corporate
Beneficial ownership declaration and AML/KYC clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank application is delayed or denied, address any AML/KYC deficiencies, including source of funds and underlying EdTech revenue model; escalate to the commercial banking centre's account manager or seek alternative access through a licensed Canadian payment facilitator that accepts limited partnership clients.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial or physical manufacturing establishment exists; general economic oversight only by the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) and Investissement Québec for innovation support programs.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for pure e-learning software operations; no certificate of authorization or manufacturing permit is issued for ISIC 6201 activities in Québec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-only activities; no industrial facility within the meaning of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2); no environmental impact assessment authorization required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 1).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation from software subscription services; municipal sewer discharge, building heating, and data-centre hosting fall outside the partnership's direct operational footprint.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c S-3.1) and applicable Montréal by-laws, with a municipal fire safety inspection for the office premises; occupational health registration with CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) and implementation of a workplace health and safety program under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1); structural load inspection not required for standard office occupancy; the building lessor must provide a valid occupancy certificate and proof of compliance with the Québec Construction Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: GST/HST: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-business-registration.html and CRA My Business Account. QST: Revenu Québec via the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ) and Revenu Québec's Clic Portfolio at https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/. The federal Business Number (BN) is the required TIN for GST/HST purposes; the NEQ is the provincial enterprise identifier used to open the QST account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and, for GST/HST, file prescribed form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and GST/HST Accounts) with the CRA; a foreign limited partnership registering for GST/HST must designate an authorized representative and provide foreign identity documents and business proof. 2. Register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and any required Quebec legal establishment records. 3. Register with Revenu Québec for the QST account using the NEQ, completing Revenu Québec form LM-1 (unless automatic registration via the Registraire linking service). 4. Provide partnership governing documentation, registered agent/power of attorney details in Quebec, and evidence of non-resident partner status where applicable. Revocation or cancellation requires filing GST/HST and QST final returns and liquidation documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian and Quebec income tax purposes under Income Tax Act subsection 96(2) and the Civil Code of Quebec partnership rules. Income, gains, losses, and investment tax credits flow through to partners, while the partnership files an information return (federal T5013 and Quebec RL-16). For GST/HST and QST, the partnership is itself a taxable 'person' and a registrant to the extent it makes taxable supplies in Canada/Quebec, and it obtains its own BN/NEQ-based tax account. Territorial scope: the LP is subject to Canadian taxation only to the extent it carries on a business or realizes taxable Canadian-source income; a non-resident partner is taxable on the partner's share of Canadian-source partnership income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box classification election equivalent to US Treasury Regulation section 301.7701-3. The limited partnership's pass-through status is statutory and mandatory. Available elections relevant to the LP: (i) subsection 249.1(6) election to adopt a partnership fiscal period matching majority interest partners; (ii) subsection 96(3) election for transfers of partnership property at agreed tax values; (iii) Excise Tax Act section 156 election to treat supplies between closely related registrants as nil consideration for GST/HST/QST purposes; and (iv) various GST/HST and QST election forms for sales, self-supply, and qualifying real property acquisitions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax), a dual VAT system in Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: Registration is mandatory once the worldwide annual taxable supplies of the registrant (excluding certain zero-rated and financial supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 for GST/HST, and the equivalent small-supplier threshold applies for QST under Revenu Québec rules. Exceptions and mandatory registration rules apply to non-residents who solicit business in Canada or supply prescribed digital services to persons in Quebec even below the threshold in specific circumstances.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing validation, or digital stamping for general EdTech B2C/B2B transactions. Registrants must issue tax invoices containing required GST/HST and QST information, preserve electronic records, and file returns electronically through CRA and Revenu Québec online filing/API channels when turnover exceeds prescribed thresholds. The Pan-Canadian Trust Framework for e-invoicing is voluntary. For App Store and Play Store sales, the taxpayer must retain Apple/Google payment reports and invoice data to document the GST/HST and QST treatment of each downloadable digital supply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated if supplied and delivered outside Canada, or subject to continuous exportation in a carrier that exports them prior to use in Canada. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated when the recipient is not present in Canada at the time the service is performed and the service is not required to be performed in Canada. Digital supply of EdTech language-learning software and automated tutoring services qualifies for zero-rating as a supply of intangible personal property or a service made to a non-resident recipient, provided the recipient receives it outside Canada and does not use it in Canada; records must evidence geographic delivery and non-resident status (e.g., IP address, billing address, app store download jurisdiction).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A/B13B) where tangible media or goods are exported
Customs export clearance record and proof of departure (carrier airway bill, bill of lading, port/customs stamp)
Commercial invoice with incoterms and HS/schedule classification
Signed contract or terms of service demonstrating non-resident buyer/tutor recipient
Country-specific digital delivery logs showing IP locations and download/access records
Payment evidence and inward remittance certificate or app store payout statements
Packing list and proof of outside-Canada destination for any tangible export component
Any certificate of origin or export permit if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated exports within the normal reassessment period (normally four years, or longer in the case of negligence/misrepresentation) and claw back the zero-rating, thereby assessing uncollected GST/HST and QST, disallowing input tax credits, and applying statutory interest. Civil penalties include false statement penalties up to 25% of the tax amount (or 50% for gross negligence), failure to file penalties of 5% plus 1% per month, and, in serious cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion with fines, imprisonment, and punitive damages. CRA may also disregard transactions under anti-avoidance rules when non-resident paper flows are merely formal and no substantive export occurred.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary and financial-stability authority. There is no centralized foreign-exchange administration; cross-border financial transaction reporting is supervised by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers cross-border currency declarations and export reporting under the Customs Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada maintains no foreign-exchange control law, no prior-approval regime for profit remittances, and no restriction on capital withdrawals or dividends by non-residents. The only material frictions are tax-driven: a non-resident limited partner receiving partnership income characterized as non-active business income is subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (base rate 25%, reduced by treaty to commonly 5-15% depending on the partner's residence). Management fees or royalties remitted to non-residents attract 25% withholding unless treaty relief is filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). For Quebec, Revenu Quebec applies the same remittance framework, and the LP must hold a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and register for GST/HST/QST where taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, conversion ratio, or mandatory repatriation timeline for export receipts. Canadian residents may freely retain foreign currency offshore or in Foreign-Currency Bank Accounts (FCBA) at authorized Canadian banks. The only binding obligations are reporting-based: (i) FINTRAC requires Canadian financial intermediaries to report every cross-border electronic funds transfer of C$10,000 or more; (ii) commercial goods exports from Canada require CBSA export reporting under the Export Reporting and Accounting Regulations when the shipment value exceeds C$2,000 or falls within controlled categories; (iii) EdTech service exports are not subject to CBSA export reporting, but subscription revenues must be included in the partnership's Canadian tax filings and, if selected in Statistics Canada's survey sample, in Balance of Payments reporting forms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority_note: For a Quebec LP, the practical operating supervisors for treasury and FX are the Bank of Canada, FINTRAC (AML/EFT reporting), and Revenu Quebec (money-services business licensing where applicable).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_regime: Full convertibility under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act; no capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_restrictions: No restriction on foreign direct investment in a Quebec LP; only post-remittance tax withholdings apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.current_account_restrictions: None for fees, royalties, or service payments; Part XIII withholding applies to payments of income to non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.profit_remittance_hurdles: No FX approval hurdle; the practical hurdle is treaty documentation (NR301 form / provincial equivalent) to avoid excess 25% withholding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_certificate_requirement: None; a simple CBSA export declaration is needed only for the physical-goods component, which does not apply to pure software subscription deliveries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_accounting: Export proceeds may be held in any currency in Canada or abroad; no mandatory conversion into CAD.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: MEDIUM. Canada does not use the EU-style EMI licence; offshore digital EMIs are lawful only as auxiliary payment processors, not as full banking rails for a Quebec LP. Any payment service provider settling CAD for the LP must be registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, if operating in Quebec, must also hold the Quebec money-services business permit administered by Revenu Quebec under the Act respecting money-services businesses. Practical blueprint: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing serve as the primary collection layer (Apple/Google treasury entities remit net proceeds in USD/EUR via SWIFT to the LP's Tier-1 Canadian bank account), while a registered Canadian PSP (e.g., Stripe Canada, PayPal Canada, or the bank's own payment gateway) handles direct web-subscription collections. Offshore EMIs cannot provide Canadian settlement accounts or CAD clearing without a Canadian MSB registration and a local presence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec LP with non-resident partners, Tier-1 Canadian banks de facto mandate in-person identity verification for at least one authorized signatory or the General Partner at a Canadian branch, supplemented by a video interview where a physical visit is impractical. Fully remote opening is available only for low-risk personal accounts or single-director domestic corporations. For the CA_LP structure, the standard requirements are: (i) a video or in-branch interview with the relationship manager; (ii) notarized or apostilled copies of passports and proof of address for all individuals with 25%+ control; (iii) a certified Certificate of Establishment from the Quebec Registraire des entreprises (Releve de l'entreprise) and the notarized Limited Partnership Agreement; and (iv) a physical visit by the General Partner's representative or a notarized verification package authenticated by a Canadian consular officer. BMO and National Bank are the most accommodating for Quebec LPs with international ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the Limited Partnership: layered GP/LP chain with unincorporated foreign partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete control-chain package: notarized Limited Partnership Agreement, Quebec Registraire des entreprises Certificate of Establishment, capital-account schedule listing every limited partner with percentage ownership, a signed organizational chart, and a beneficial-ownership declaration reconciled against FINTRAC CDR (Client Due Diligence) extraction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner nexus and subscriber traffic originating from sanctions-covered jurisdictions (UN/EU/OFAC/Canada consolidated sanctions lists).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal sanctions-compliance policy, automated screening output against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list and OFAC SDN list, geographic IP-blocking proof, subscriber jurisdiction analytics, and a written attestation that no sanctioned counterparty participates in the LP capital stack or payment flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value micro-transactions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flagged as unexplained digital-wallet or card receivables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google payout reconciliation statements mapped to the bank ledger, platform transaction register with SKU-level detail, refund and chargeback policy, IFRS 15 revenue-recognition memo, and a signed statement of commercial model confirming NAICS 611710 (language instruction) and ISIC 6201 (software publishing).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection funded from a non-resident General Partner's personal wealth or corporate treasury without formal partnership records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds packet: executed capital-call resolution, GP board or partner resolution authorizing the transfer, bank statements of the remitting entity covering the funding window, certified partnership capital-account statement, and — where the GP is a foreign entity — a legal opinion and apostilled excerpt from the GP's home registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flow mismatch: USD subscription inflows under Apple/Google versus USD vendor disbursements for hosting, LLM licensing, and content production.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed vendor agreements, commercial invoices, SWIFT MT103 payment records, OECD transfer-pricing documentation where any vendor is affiliated, and a group treasury cash-flow model tracing each USD disbursement to a stated contractual purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all non-resident capital contributions as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers (or MT202 for bank-to-bank cover) into a segregated capital-injection/operating account at a Tier-1 Canadian bank. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state: CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_LP LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT DATED [DATE], using ISO 20022 purpose code QUASICAPITAL or CAPT so the beneficiary bank classifies the flow as equity rather than trade or debt. All transfers equal to or exceeding C$10,000 are automatically reported to FINTRAC by the receiving bank. Large inward direct investments may additionally be captured by Statistics Canada Balance of Payments surveys. Supporting documents for the receiving bank: executed capital-call resolution, GP authorization, source-of-funds evidence, a capital-account statement certified by the partnership accountant before drawdown, and, where US partners are present, a US tax characterization memo (PFIC/partnership analysis) included in the KYC file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Core clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for all external vendor payables, with USD/EUR clearing executed by the Canadian bank's corresponding banking network (US and European correspondents); (ii) CAD payables to Canadian vendors cleared through Payments Canada Lynx RTGS (high value) and ACSS (retail ACH); (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT707/MT720 where deferred-payment trade finance is required for content or licensing procurement; (iv) corporate purchasing cards for low-value SaaS and subscription tooling; and (v) FX conversion executed on the spot market by the bank's treasury desk on the same value date as the MT103 to eliminate the float and dual-currency mismatch from Apple/Google settlement cycles (Apple payouts approximately T+45 days; Google approximately T+30 days). Apple IAP and Google Play Billing remit net proceeds in USD/EUR through Apple Distribution International (Ireland) and Google Payment entities; these must be documented to the bank as on-behalf-of third-party processor flows. If physical goods (books, devices) are later embedded in the language-learning product, the LP must comply with CBSA exporter reporting under the Customs Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forward contracts (tenors 1W to 12M; bilateral ISDA or Canadian Master Derivative Agreement with the bank)
FX swaps (forward-forward rollovers to align staggered Apple/Google USD payout timing with CAD operating-expense cycles)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD longer-dated hedges used if the LP enters multi-year pre-paid subscription contracts or partner loans)
Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (costless structures to protect the budgeted USD-to-CAD conversion floor for the core operating budget)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available in principle but non-market-standard for CAD because the Canadian dollar is freely deliverable offshore; only used where an offshore hedging counterparty imposes settlement-currency constraints

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) — limited partnership renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than the last day of the calendar month corresponding to the anniversary of the LP's original REQ registration; REQ sends a reminder before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual declaration remains unfiled after the due date and after the REQ default notice, the registraire may administratively strike the LP from the enterprise register. A struck-off LP loses the benefit of registered legal publicity, cannot obtain REQ certificates, and must regularize its registration before resuming normal operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, including T5013 Summary and partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the LP's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, the due date is May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per late day, capped at CAD 2,500 and subject to a CAD 100 minimum; CRA may also impose separate penalties for failure to issue T5013 partner slips and for repeated late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return (TP-600) and related partner schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the LP's fiscal period end, aligned with the federal T5013 due date for a Quebec partnership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing to Revenu Québec can trigger administrative penalties of CAD 25 per late day, subject to a minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, plus separate penalties for missing partner information slips or failure to respond to Revenu Québec default notices.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit attaches to a private Quebec limited partnership solely because of its legal form, revenue, or asset size. An audit becomes compulsory if the partnership agreement or an investor, lender, or regulator condition requires it, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer or is otherwise subject to a statutory licence; the corporate general partner may also be required to appoint an auditor under the Quebec Business Corporations Act if shareholder approval is not waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements, if prepared, must follow Canadian generally accepted accounting principles: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises, or ASPE for private enterprises; Quebec tax filings and partnership allocation schedules are reconciled to the accounting net income under the Taxation Act and the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Quebec limited partnership has no issued share capital, so no annual UBO confirmation applies to share transfers. The annual confirmation is satisfied through the REQ annual declaration and through the general partner's internal certification that the register of limited partners and the minute book are current. Any transfer of a limited partnership interest must be recorded in the LP's internal transfer ledger; if the general partner is a Quebec or CBCA corporation, that corporate general partner must maintain and annually confirm its individual-with-significant-control register under applicable corporate law.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (limited partners), including names, addresses, contributions, withdrawals and transfer history
Register of Directors (or general partner register) and officer appointments
Minute Book containing resolutions of the general partner and annual approval of financial statements
